Title: MARC upgrades SAJ Capital sukuk, outlook stable
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has upgraded SAJ Capital Sdn Bhd's sukuk Murabahah programme of up to RM650 million to AAIS from AA-IS, with a stable outlook.
SAJ Capital is a wholly-owned funding vehicle of Ranhill Capital Sdn Bhd, which owns an 80 per cent stake in Ranhill SAJ, Johor's sole source-to-tap water services provider.
Given its reliance on dividends from Ranhill SAJ to meet its sukuk obligations, SAJ Capital's rating is driven by Ranhill SAJ's credit strength.
MARC said the upgrade reflects Ranhill SAJ's materially stronger credit profile, underpinned by sustained improvements in operating performance, cash flow generation and financial flexibility.
"This strengthening has been driven by rising water demand and the tariff adjustments implemented in 2024 and 2025, which have resulted in stronger earnings, liquidity and debt-servicing capacity," it said.
MARC also expects Johor's expanding economy, ongoing industrialisation and growing data centre investments to sustain long- term growth in water demand and resilient cash flow generation.
Based on Ranhill SAJ's financial performance for the first nine months of the financial year (FY26), MARC projects full-year revenue to reach about RM1.9 billion, representing an increase of more than 30 per cent compared with historical levels.
Operating cash flow is expected to improve to around RM800 million, underpinned by consistently strong earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) margins of between 41 per cent and 54 per cent over the past five years.
MARC said the stronger earnings and operating cash flow have enhanced Ranhill SAJ's liquidity, capital position and financial flexibility, enabling sustainable dividend distributions to SAJ Capital.
It expects dividend flows to remain sufficient to support SAJ Capital's sukuk obligations, with the financial service coverage ratio projected to average around 2.0 times between FY27 and FY30, comfortably above the sukuk covenant requirement of 1.5 times.
Outstanding sukuk under the programme stood at RM300 million as at end-June 2026.

Title: Malaysian arrested in Singapore with 9kg cannabis, 530g meth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 22-year-old Malaysian man has been arrested in Singapore for attempting to smuggle drugs worth about RM1.15 million into the republic.
The suspect, from Johor, was detained with about 9kg of cannabis and 530g of methamphetamine.
The case follows recent arrests of Malaysians abroad, including a pilot and another man in Indonesia, for similar drug trafficking activities.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police had received information on the arrest and had launched follow-up investigations to identify those behind the cross-border syndicate.

Title: UK PM Burnham considering inquiry into Epstein, minister says
Article:
LONDON: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is looking at holding a public inquiry into the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and his actions in the UK, victims minister Alex Davies-Jones told the BBC.
Nearly seven years after his death, the Epstein scandal has rocked the British establishment, leading to the arrest of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, King Charles' brother, and of Peter Mandelson, the former British ambassador to the US.
Burnham, who became prime minister in July, will meet Epstein's victims, Davies-Jones told BBC Newsnight, and a public inquiry could follow.
"We are looking into this. We are seeing what is possible," the minister said.
British police are already investigating a number of allegations related to the disgraced financier, with possible offences ranging from child sex abuse to trafficking women through UK airports and misconduct in public office.
Davies-Jones said any public inquiry could also examine the alleged actions of the late Egyptian billionaire Mohamed al-Fayed, another public figure who has been accused of rape and sexual assault by hundreds of victims.
In another report, US Democratic Senator Ron Wyden called for federal regulators to probe big banks over their handling of Epstein's accounts after surfacing what Wyden said was potential evidence that the banks failed to report suspicious transactions linked to the late convicted ​sex offender.
In a report released on Tuesday, Wyden alleged that Bank of America, Deutsche Bank and JPMorgan Chase may have violated federal anti-money laundering laws by failing to report Epstein's suspicious transactions in a timely manner.
Wyden's four-year investigation included a review of so-called suspicious activity reports (SARs) which banks file to the Treasury Department, materials from lawsuits and court filings, and information the senator sought from Wall Street banks and the U.S. Treasury.
Bank of America failed to properly screen and report US$170 million in payments to Epstein, Wyden's report said, adding that the bank years later concluded in suspicious activity reports that the transactions had no verifiable business purpose.
"We take our legal and regulatory obligations seriously and, as we have previously said, the bank did not facilitate wrongdoing," a BofA spokesperson said.
[[nid:1504677]]
Deutsche Bank failed to report on time more than US$250 million in suspicious wire transfers tied to Epstein, including payments to women in Russia and other parts of Eastern Europe, the report said.
Deutsche Bank said in a statement that it takes its legal obligations seriously and regrets its historical connection with Epstein.
Wyden's report also alleged that JPMorgan delayed reporting over US$1 billion in suspicious Epstein-linked transfers to the Treasury, including payments to women in Russia and Belarus.
A spokesperson for the bank said this was false. "We began flagging suspicious transactions for the government as early as 2002 and throughout our relationship...even after we closed his accounts," she said.
"We acted appropriately on what we knew, when we knew it, as the law requires."
Epstein was a JPMorgan client from 1998 until the bank cut him off in 2013, years after he pleaded guilty to prostitution-related charges. Deutsche took him on as a client in 2013 after JPMorgan closed his accounts.
"We have cooperated with regulatory and law enforcement agencies regarding their investigations and have been transparent in addressing deficiencies and investing in strengthening our control environment in parallel," a Deutsche Bank spokesperson said.
Reuters couldn't verify the details of the report.
An administration official said Treasury does not comment on investigations, including to confirm or deny whether one exists. Treasury has fully cooperated with valid requests for information from Congress, the official said.
Epstein died in a Manhattan ​jail cell in August 2019 while awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges.

Title: Shafee seeks to strike out parts of Tony Pua's statement in 1MDB suit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah has applied to expunge large portions of former DAP lawmaker Tony Pua's witness statement in the US$5.64 billion 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) civil suit against Datuk Seri Najib Razak and several others.
The senior lawyer, who is representing Najib, argued that Pua was giving evidence "as though he is the chief investigator", almost like the Inspector-General of Police, despite relying on matters he allegedly knew only through second-hand sources.
At the outset of today's hearing, Shafee said the former Damansara MP's statement was largely based on hearsay and personal opinion.
He said the defence had no objection to portions of Pua's statement relating to his direct involvement in the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), where Pua had participated in the committee's examination of 1MDB and questioning of its directors and officers.
However, Shafee objected to sections where Pua offered his views on the PAC proceedings, the government's handling of the 1MDB investigations and why Najib was not interviewed by the committee.
"All this is opinion. He is giving evidence as though he is the chief investigator, almost in the position of the IGP, on matters that he only knows from second-hand sources. In fact, he is merely a second-hand source," he said.
Shafee said Pua should not substitute his personal account for official records, particularly where the matters could be established through the PAC report or parliamentary proceedings.
He cited Pua's claims that the PAC did not have full access to necessary documents and that Najib was not interviewed, as well as assertions that bank statements belonging to 1MDB and its foreign subsidiaries, and documents identifying the ownership of Good Star Limited, were not provided to the committee.
Shafee argued that if such matters were recorded in the PAC report or proceedings, the official documents should be tendered instead of relying on Pua's personal account.
He also challenged Pua's claim that suggestions by opposition PAC members were rejected by members of the then ruling coalition, saying it was unclear whether the account was based on official proceedings or informal discussions.
Shafee further objected to Pua's reliance on media reports, as well as statements by the Malaysian Bar, Bank Negara Malaysia, foreign authorities and the United States Department of Justice's forfeiture complaints.
He said such material could not be treated as proof of the allegations contained in them and that the relevant parties should instead be called as witnesses for cross-examination.
Shafee also questioned Pua's reliance on investigations conducted in Singapore, Hong Kong and Switzerland, including a Swiss request for mutual legal assistance over the alleged misappropriation of about US$4 billion from 1MDB.
"Where he relies on Hansard, I have no objection. But where he relies on media reports, those are inadmissible," he said.
He maintained that a witness of fact should testify only on matters within personal knowledge, rather than provide opinions or submissions.
Lawyer Lee Shih, representing the plaintiffs, said Pua was not being called to establish the truth of allegations contained in media reports.
Instead, he said the references were meant to show that certain events, parliamentary statements, PAC proceedings and reports had taken place, as well as to describe the political climate surrounding 1MDB at the time.
Lee then asked judicial commissioner Mohamad Redzuan Idrus to adjourn proceedings to allow time to prepare written submissions in response to Shafee's application. The court allowed the adjournment.
The hearing will continue tomorrow.

Title: Girl's viral video in car with missing rear windshield brings help to family
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A viral video showing a young girl waving at motorists from a car without a rear windshield has led social activist Adrian Edy to a family struggling with financial hardship.
The encounter with the family of seven taught the 30-year-old a valuable lesson about finding happiness despite living a modest life, after the father whom he called 'Pakcik Ambarat' told him he remained grateful for his old second-hand Proton Iswara despite being unable to work.
"When we were eating together yesterday, Pakcik Ambarat told me that he was still grateful to have his old second-hand Proton Iswara, which he bought seven years ago.
"Apart from that, due to a foot injury sustained in March, he has been unable to work at construction sites and occasionally struggles to provide for his family of seven," the 30-year-old told the New Straits Times.
Adrian, a local, has been carrying out solo humanitarian efforts to help underprivileged communities.
Recently, a video of Ambarat's third child went viral after the 6-year-old girl was seen sitting at the back of their car and waving at other motorists.
The car was missing its rear windshield.
Adrian said the glass had shattered on its own while the vehicle was parked at home due to its age.
"Upon learning about the incident, I reached out to the public to help me track down the family as I wanted to assist them in repairing the car.
"A staff member from a car workshop in Putatan contacted me after learning that I was looking for them.
"The great thing is that they also offered to replace the glass, change the engine oil and service the air conditioner, which I estimated would cost around RM1,000," he said.
He added that since the repair costs were sponsored by the workshop he contributed some pocket money, a food basket and a capybara plushie for the family.
He hoped the assistance would help ease the family's burden.

Title: GOF records 813 arrests involving various enforcement operations in 4 states
Article:
IPOH: The Northern Brigade of the General Operations Force (GOF) recorded 813 arrests involving various enforcement operations in Perak, Penang, Kedah, and Perlis as of Aug 4 this year, compared to 672 arrests during the same period last year.
Its commander, SAC Balveer Singh Mahindar Singh, said that in the same period the total number of cases also increased to 389 cases compared to 291 cases recorded during the same period last year, which is an increase of 98 cases or 33.68 per cent.
"This proves the effective strategic collaboration between officers and personnel of the Northern Brigade GOF, continuous intelligence, and information provided by the public in strengthening enforcement actions," he said at a press conference here today.
Commenting on the operational achievements, Balveer Singh said the Integrated Khazanah Operation, carried out in collaboration with the Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan); the Forestry Department, Minerals and Geoscience Department, and the Land and Mines Office, recorded 38 cases this year compared to 17 cases during the same period last year.
"The operation also recorded 63 arrests compared to 27 arrests in the previous year, while the value of the seizures increased dramatically from RM2.27 million to RM56.86 million, which is an increase of about 2,404 per cent," he said.
For roadblock operations conducted in seven locations in northern Peninsular Malaysia, Balveer Singh said that 75 cases were recorded this year compared to 24 cases during the same period last year.
He said the operations also recorded 89 arrests, an increase from 30 arrests last year, or a 196 per cent increase.
Meanwhile, Balveer Singh said that for cases under the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (Atipsom), 11 cases were recorded this year compared to six cases during the same period last year.
He said that the number of arrests under the Act increased from 12 to 14 people, while the value of the seizures also increased from RM308,000 to RM465,000 during the same period.
Therefore, Balveer Singh emphasised that the Northern Brigade GOF will continue to strengthen inter-agency cooperation, enhance intelligence gathering, and optimise information sharing with the public to combat various forms of crime in the northern region of the country.

Title: Prison officer arrested over RM3,000 bribe to smuggle contraband into jail
Article:
AYER KEROH: A prison officer has been arrested over allegations of soliciting and accepting about RM3,000 in bribes to smuggle prohibited items into a prison.
A Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) source said the suspect was arrested at about 11.50am yesterday at his home in Sungai Petani, Kedah.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect, in his 20s, allegedly committed the offence in March while serving at a prison in Melaka.

Title: RM10.68m drug-laced vape syndicate busted in Johor, seven arrested
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Police crippled a syndicate processing and distributing drug-infused vape cartridges worth RM10.68 million following the arrest of seven suspects, in five simultaneous raids across the state on Sunday.
Johor deputy police chief Deputy Commissioner Hoo Chuan Huat said the suspects, aged between 36 and 46, comprised six men, including a foreign man and a foreign woman.
He said the first raid at a petrol station at the Kulai Rest and Relax (R&R) area led to the arrest of the Malaysian man and foreign woman.
"An inspection of a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) uncovered 9,000 vape cartridges containing suspected liquid methamphetamine weighing 82.40kg, with an estimated value of RM4.12 million.
"The second raid in Bandar Medini, Iskandar Puteri, led to the arrest of the foreign man at a condominium unit used as a storage and filling facility for the drug-infused vape cartridges," he told a press conference at the Johor police contingent headquarters here today.
Hoo said following that raid, police seized 47 plastic bottles containing vape flavours, a glass bottle containing 127.55 litres of liquid methamphetamine worth RM6.37 million, two packets of cocaine weighing 410g, a packet of ketamine weighing 40g, as well as machines and equipment used to fill the vape cartridges.
Meanwhile, he said the third raid in Taman Sutera Utama here led to the arrest of another local man and the seizure of 11.45g of heroin, 20 Erimin 5 pills, and 53 ecstasy pills.
"The fourth raid in Mutiara Rini and the fifth raid at a petrol station parking lot in Tanjung Agas, Muar, led to the arrest of three more men.
"In total, the operation resulted in the seizure of 210.43kg of various drugs worth RM10.68 million, which could have been used by 649,096 addicts," he said.
He added that investigations revealed that the syndicate had been active since February, using the condominium to package and fill the liquid drugs into vape cartridges before distributing them to the local market.
"Investigations found that the first suspect acted as a transporter, the second suspect who is his wife assisted in the operations, the third suspect managed the store, the fourth suspect acted as a runner, the fifth suspect was the recipient of the packages, the sixth suspect was an assistant and the seventh suspect is believed to be the mastermind or leader of the syndicate," he said.
He added that two suspects tested positive for methamphetamine following urine tests, while four others had previous records for crime and drug-related offences.
He said all suspects have been remanded for seven until Aug 9 to assist in investigations under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.

Title: Bersatu tells Azeez to clarify if MACC contacted him over TH RCI findings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu has called on former Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim to clarify whether he has been summoned or contacted by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) over findings from the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into the institution.
The party's supreme council member Dr Afif Bahardin said Azeez, who had claimed to have a 2021 letter from the MACC chief commissioner clearing him of any involvement, must make the document public.
"The people have the right to know the true status of this matter, and any speculation can only be stopped through an open explanation from him and a clean and independent investigation process," he said in a statement.
Afif also called on the MACC and the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) to carry out investigations and make any prosecution decisions independently, professionally and without bias.
The RCI report on TH, which was declassified last week, revealed that the fund's financial position was
in a critical state
in 2017.
This followed losses at the institution — which manages savings and haj affairs for Malaysian Muslims — mounting to RM10 billion, forcing the government to implement a recovery plan as a matter of urgency.

Title: High Court acquits temple chairman, quashes trespass charge
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A temple chairman was acquitted by the High Court today after it quashed a criminal trespass charge against him, ruling that it failed to disclose the necessary element of intent.
Lawyer Latheefa Koya, in a statement, said judge Dr Hazlina Hussain found that the charge against M. Paramaguru, 49, did not state that he had the intention to commit an offence, a key ingredient of criminal trespass.
She said the judge ruled that allowing the case to proceed to trial would be a waste of judicial time as the charge contained an incurable defect.
In February, Paramaguru, who is also a security guard, pleaded not guilty at the magistrate's court in Sepang to a charge of trespassing onto land belonging to Suhaili Ahmad without permission.
The alleged offence was said to have taken place at 4.45pm on June 19 last year.
He was charged under Section 447 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of six months, a fine of up to RM3,000, or both upon conviction.
Latheefa, who appeared with lawyer Rajesh Nagarajan, said the defence had applied to strike out the charge on the grounds that it failed to allege the intention to commit an offence.
"To charge a person for criminal trespass, you have to show the intention to commit an offence, and that was missing in the charge.
"The mere act of trespassing onto land is essentially a civil matter. If you are a landowner and someone trespasses on your land, that alone does not amount to a criminal offence," she said.
She said the prosecution had argued that the element of intent could be established during the trial.
Deputy public prosecutor Mohammed Heikal Ismail confirmed the High Court's ruling.
Speaking after the proceedings, Paramaguru said he was relieved by the decision and maintained that he had not trespassed onto the land.
Instead, he said he had gone to the Sri Maha Mariamman Temple located on the land to perform his daily prayers with other devotees.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kulasegaran: Security laws must not erode human rights
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Efforts to strengthen national security must not come at the expense of human rights, Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister's Department for Law and Institutional Reform M. Kulasegaran said.
He said both priorities must advance together through an effective, balanced and forward-looking legal framework.
"The question is not whether the country needs tougher or more lenient laws, but how to develop a legal framework that protects national security without compromising the rule of law and human rights.
"Legal reform had become increasingly important as technology, society and security threats continued to evolve. Reform does not mean existing laws have failed.
It is a continuous process of improvement to ensure legislation remains relevant to technological developments, social change and emerging challenges," he said in his keynote address at a symposium on national security-related crimes and the effectiveness of current laws in addressing present and future threats at Parliament House today.
Present were National Security Council director-general Datuk Raja Nushirwan Zainal Abidin and Dewan Negara Special Select Committee on Law Review chairman Senator Rita Sarimah Patrick Insol.
Kulasegaran said the changing landscape of security threats, which now includes cyber attacks and the misuse of technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), requires the country's legal framework to be always responsive to current challenges.
However, he said in strengthening national security, every action must remain based on the Federal Constitution, the rule of law and the principles of justice.
"No single institution can confront national security threats alone. National security requires whole-of-government and whole-of-society approaches involving the government, Parliament, the private sector, academia, civil society and the public," he said.
Earlier, Rita Sarimah, in her welcoming speech, said security threats were no longer confined to military matters or border defence, as they now included cybercrime, disinformation, extremism, espionage, foreign interference, attacks on critical infrastructure and the misuse of emerging technologies.
As such, she said the country's legal framework must evolve with these developments to ensure national security remained protected.
"The question is not whether national security laws must change, but how far those changes should go to keep them relevant, effective and capable of meeting the country's future needs," she said.
Rita Sarimah said modern security risks were also shaped by hybrid threats combining physical, digital, economic, psychological and geopolitical elements, which had prompted many countries to review their security laws while preserving democracy, the rule of law and human rights.
She said the Dewan Negara, as the upper house of Parliament, played an important check-and-balance role by scrutinising policies and legislation in a thorough, objective and forward-looking manner.
The Special Select Committee on Law Review, she added, conducted independent, professional and evidence-based reviews of existing laws to identify improvements for the government and Parliament to consider.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah police need to leverage technology, says state police chief
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah police must leverage technological advancements to improve work efficiency, particularly in investigations and the preparation of investigation papers, said state police commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun.
He said that early in his career, most tasks, including preparing investigation papers, were carried out manually and took longer to complete.
He cited a murder case he handled early in his career which took up to seven days to investigate as the process was done manually.
"In the past, I opened about 50 investigation papers a month involving index and non-index cases.
"Today, investigating officers can handle more than 200 investigation papers with the help of modern systems.
"Use the available facilities to speed up investigations so that the public receives justice faster," he said during the rank-pinning and handover of duties ceremony for the Kota Kinabalu police chief.
The ceremony saw Superintendent Syed Lot Syed Abdul Rahman hand over duties as Kota Kinabalu district police chief to Assistant Commissioner Shahrudin Mat Husain..
Meanwhile, Jauteh reminded personnel to accept every instruction and change introduced with an open mind.
"Do not say that new directives are wrong or unsuitable. I want everyone to cooperate and accept the changes introduced for the betterment of the force.
"We need to unite and work as a team to ensure that every policy introduced can be implemented effectively," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: India monsoon floods, landslides kill more than 100 since July
Article:
NEW DELHI: Floods and landslides triggered by monsoon rains have killed more than 100 people across India since July, official data showed Wednesday, with thousands forced to flee their inundated homes.
While the annual monsoon brings rainfall that farmers depend on, scientists say climate change is making the phenomenon more erratic, unpredictable and deadly across the South Asia region.
India's northeastern state of Assam is among the hardest hit by the annual rains, with at least 87 people killed, according to Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma.
In the state's worst-affected Sivasagar district, some 47 people have been killed as several areas remain under water.
State authorities have appealed for financial donations from the public to support relief and rehabilitation efforts.
"The devastation here is unlike anything these areas have witnessed before," Sarma posted on X.
"Material losses can be restored, but no compensation can replace a loved one."
AFP images showed residents using rafts and inflated boats to reach higher ground with the help of the state's disaster response officials.
In India's southern state of Kerala, Chief Minister VD Satheesan said at least 15 people have been killed and another seven were missing after heavy rains over several days.
More than 300 relief camps have been set up in the state, sheltering over 10,000 people, after rains triggered landslides and swollen rivers breached their banks.
In the Himalayan territory of Jammu and Kashmir, at least 31 people been killed, according to a report by the public state broadcaster.
Monsoon-related disasters are an annual occurrence across India after the region's long summers when many parts of the country face water scarcity and drought.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tech stocks dominate Bursa again amid fresh optimism
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian technology stocks returned to the spotlight on Wednesday as investors latched onto fresh optimism that proposed United States restrictions on Chinese optical transceivers could benefit local manufacturers.
The rally extended gains from last Friday, when Bursa Malaysia's technology sector tracked a powerful overnight surge in Wall Street technology stocks led by Microsoft.
By the midday break, the Bursa Malaysia Technology Index had climbed 2.91 per cent to 77.83, its highest level since July 18, 2024. It was the best-performing sectoral index, while the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI rose 0.93 per cent to 1,748.84.
Technology and technology-linked counters dominated the exchange's most active list, led by NationGate Holdings Bhd, Inari Amertron Bhd, Zetrix AI Bhd, VS Industry Bhd and SNS Network Technology Bhd.
NationGate and VS Industry, both electronics manufacturing services providers, gained on expectations that any shift in production away from China could create opportunities for manufacturers in Malaysia.
NationGate, the market's most actively traded stock, rose 6.2 per cent to RM1.37. VS Industry, the fourth most active counter, added 4.35 per cent to 24 sen. Both are components of Bursa Malaysia Industrial Products and Services Index.
Among technology counters, Inari climbed to its highest level in more than eight months after nearly 40 million shares changed hands. The stock rose as much as 9.1 per cent before easing to RM2.39, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM8.4 billion.
Zetrix AI, formerly MyEG Services Bhd, bucked the broader rally, slipping 2.04 per cent to 72 sen. It was the third most actively traded stock on Bursa Malaysia.
SNS Network, an information and communications technology solutions provider, was Bursa Malaysia's fifth most actively traded counter. It closed the morning session unchanged at 55.5 sen after touching a six-month high of 58 sen earlier in the day.
The renewed interest in technology stocks came as global investors rotated back into artificial intelligence (AI)-linked plays.
Strong earnings and upbeat outlooks from Microsoft, Amazon and data analytics firm Palantir eased concerns over heavy AI spending and the timeline for returns, AFP reported.
Meanwhile, news reports said the US government is working on measures to block imports of new Chinese optical transceivers, which are used to transmit data through fibre-optic cables in data centres.
The proposed restrictions have fuelled expectations that production could increasingly shift to manufacturers outside China, potentially benefiting companies across Malaysia's semiconductor and electronics supply chain.
Following this, China's CSI300 Telecommunication Services Index fell six per cent in early trade, while export-oriented optical component makers Zhongji Innolight, Eoptolink Technology and Suzhou TFC Optical Communications all opened sharply lower.
Zhongji Innolight, which derived 62 per cent of its first-quarter revenue from the US market, fell about eight per cent in both Shanghai and Hong Kong trading, Reuters reported.
Back home,
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said
Malaysian technology companies with exposure to the optical transceiver supply chain could emerge as beneficiaries as geopolitical tensions accelerate the shift of manufacturing away from China.
The research house said the US' proposed restrictions on new Chinese-made optical transceiver models could reinforce the "China+1" strategy, prompting more production to move to Southeast Asia, Taiwan and the US.
Chinese manufacturers account for more than half of global optical transceiver supply. However, global players such as Coherent and Lumentum have already established manufacturing operations and are expanding capacity in Southeast Asia, HLIB said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US cooling giant picks Nilai for US$150mil plant
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: US-based sustainable cooling solutions provider BAC will invest US$150 million to establish a new manufacturing facility in Nilai, Negri Sembilan.
Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) said the investment is expected to create up to 200 high-skilled jobs by 2035, including high-skilled engineering and professional roles.
The project was marked by a groundbreaking ceremony today, attended by Mida deputy chief executive officer (Investment Development) Zuaida Abdullah, BAC president Don Fetzer and BAC global vice president and Asia Pacific head Ted Lim.
It will be developed in two phases on a 7.36 hectare site.
Phase one, targeted for completion by the end of 2027, will comprise a 30,000 square-metre manufacturing facility and a regional engineering and manufacturing office.
The second phase will establish a research and development centre and introduce more advanced manufacturing technologies, with the core manufacturing facility expected to be fully completed by 2030.
According to Mida, the Nilai facility will house BAC's latest climate-controlled product development and testing laboratory in Asia Pacific.
"The laboratory will enable local engineering teams to develop, test and validate cooling technologies for tropical climates and high-density applications.
"Combined with Malaysia's skilled workforce, this will strengthen BAC's regional engineering capabilities and support continued product innovation," it said.
Zuaida said the investment by the US-based company reflects growing confidence in Malaysia as a preferred destination for high-value, sustainable manufacturing.
"This investment embodies the 'multiplier effect' we aim to cultivate - generating high-skilled engineering jobs for Malaysian talent and opening new supply chain doors for our local small and medium enterprises as well as supporting the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 and our National Energy Transition Roadmap," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCMC, chairman reach out-of-court defamation settlement with Chegubard
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and its chairman, Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din, have agreed to an out-of-court settlement in a defamation suit against blogger Badrul Hisham Shaharin, better known as Chegubard.
The defamation suit was filed by the MCMC and its chairman at the Seremban High Court on May 14, 2025, over a post made by Badrul on his Facebook account.
Lawyer Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, who represented Badrul, said the parties agreed to seek a resolution through a mediation session conducted today.
"Actually, the trial for this case was scheduled for four days from Aug 10 to 13 at the Seremban High Court.
"However, both parties were instructed to go to the Mediation Centre to see if they could find common ground and a resolution. Alhamdulillah, today, both parties agreed," he said when met at the Seremban Court Complex.
Rafique, who was assisted by lawyers Muhammad Amirul Ar Rasyid Azman and Akif Rusli, said the terms of the agreement would be recorded at the Seremban High Court on Aug 10 before Judge Mohamad Haldar Abdul Aziz.
"So, at that time we will reveal and state what the terms of the settlement are," he said.
He said the out-of-court settlement was made as the parties sought to save costs without wasting the court's time and energy, as well as that of all parties involved.
"Because we feel there is a need for other cases to be given priority over this case. So, we will meet at the Seremban High Court on Aug 10.
"The terms being recorded and finalized between the parties will be clearly informed at 11am on Aug 10," he said.
Lawyers Nurshafiqa Balqish Jaffri and C. Sudha represented the MCMC and its chairman during today's mediation session.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nine more open spaces gazetted to strengthen KL's green space protection
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is stepping up efforts to safeguard Kuala Lumpur's green spaces with the gazettement of nine additional open areas, aimed at ensuring city development remains balanced while preserving public recreational areas.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the latest gazettement was carried out by the Federal Territories Department and the Federal Territories Director of Lands and Mines Office, covering a total area of 5.15ha or 51,502sqm.
She said the move means 552 open space lots have now been gazetted across Kuala Lumpur, spanning 468.36ha (4.68 million square metres), an area comparable to around 655 football fields or almost 1.4 times the size of Perdana Botanical Gardens.
"Gazettement goes beyond an administrative exercise. It reinforces the protection of open spaces so they can continue serving as public areas for recreation, leisure and community activities, while minimising the risk of future land-use changes," she said in a Facebook post today.
She said every gazetted area represents more space for children to play, families to spend leisure time, senior citizens to exercise, and communities to enjoy a greener, healthier and more comfortable urban environment.
The nine newly gazetted open spaces include Lot 82448 in the Batu sub-district, near Desa ParkCity Lake (6,607sqm or 1.632 acres); Lot 82443 in the Batu sub-district, also near Desa ParkCity Lake (22,000sqm or 5.436 acres); Lot 202030 in the Setapak sub-district, near Bayu Sentul Condominium (13,882 square metres or 3.430 acres); and Lot 38500 in the Petaling sub-district, near Residensi Jalil Mas (529 square metres or 0.130 acres).
Other newly gazetted open spaces include Lot 25119 in the Setapak sub-district, near Masjid Salahuddin Al-Ayubbi in Taman Melati (1,456sqm or 0.359 acres); Lot 39399 in the Petaling sub-district, near East Bukit Jalil Condominium (1,658 square metres or 0.409 acres); Lot 39397 in the Petaling sub-district, also near East Bukit Jalil Condominium (185 sqm or 0.045 acres); Lot 56219 in the Batu sub-district, near United Point Mall (3,679sqm); and Lot 482950 in the Kuala Lumpur suib-district, near Padang TURF Tasik Permaisuri (1,505 sqm or 0.371 acres).
Yeoh said the public can access details of gazetted open spaces via the MyHijau portal on the Federal Territories Director of Lands and Mines Office's official website, enabling Kuala Lumpur residents to play a role in monitoring and safeguarding the city's green areas.
"The gazettement of the nine additional areas reflects the Madani government's ongoing commitment to balanced urban development in Kuala Lumpur, while safeguarding public recreational spaces, community well-being and the city's climate resilience," she said.

Title: Body found in a net: Two more men arrested
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Police have arrested two more men over the murder of a man whose body was found bound and wrapped in a net in Sungai Tanjung, Parit Raja, on Sunday.
Johor deputy police chief Deputy Commissioner Hoo Chuan Huat said the suspects, aged 33 and 34, were picked up in Kluang and Johor Baru yesterday.
This brings the total number of arrests in the case to five.
"The three suspects arrested earlier have been remanded for seven days until Aug 10, while the two suspects arrested yesterday have also been remanded until the same date," he told a press conference.
Hoo said investigations were ongoing and did not rule out the involvement of other suspects.
He said preliminary investigations indicated the motive was linked to a debt dispute, though each suspect's role in the murder had yet to be determined.
"So far, it is believed that one of the suspects owed money to the victim, while the others are believed to be associates," he said, adding that police were awaiting the post-mortem report.
The victim's body was found floating in the river on Sunday.
The case is being probed under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder, which carries the death penalty or a jail term of between 30 and 40 years, and no fewer than 12 strokes of the rotan.

Title: Asian stocks hit multi-week highs as easing US-Iran tensions lift risk appetite
Article:
SINGAPORE: Most emerging Asian equities climbed to multi-week highs and regional currencies strengthened on Wednesday as hopes of easing US-Iran tensions boosted risk appetite and kept oil prices below US$80 a barrel.
The MSCI emerging markets Asia equities index rose about three per cent to a two-week high, while the EM currencies gauge gained 0.4 per cent to an all-time high.
Crude futures steadied after a two-day slide, supported by hopes for a Middle East ceasefire and progress in discussions to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key global shipping route.
"Overall, markets are trying their best to look through any potential re-ignition in the conflict towards the final destination – and perhaps rightly so," Michael Wan, MUFG senior currency analyst, said in a note.
Crude prices have been far more benign than headline supply disruptions indicate, with some of the resilience in the system helped by a much sharper-than-expected drop in oil imports from China, Wan added.
South Korea's KOSPI surged as much as five per cent, lifted by gains in chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix after an overnight rally in US AI-linked stocks.
Taiwan's tech-heavy benchmark followed suit, jumping 3.4 per cent. Equities in Kuala Lumpur advanced as much as one per cent to their highest point since mid-May and were on track for a sixth session of gains.
Bangkok shares climbed as much as 0.8 per cent before trimming some gains. Thailand's headline inflation rose less than expected in July, weighed by lower oil prices. The Singapore bourse bucked the regional trend, falling as much as 0.8 per cent to its lowest level in more than a week.
The FTSE Straits Times index was on track for a fifth consecutive session of declines, moving further away from its record high of 5,713.19 reached on July 29.
In currency markets, the South Korean won, Taiwan dollar and Philippine peso, all sensitive to energy prices, strengthened modestly.
The Indonesian rupiah moved back below the closely watched 18,000-per-dollar level and was last trading at 17,935 per US dollar. The Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar were the only major emerging Asian currencies to remain little changed on the day.
The rupee pared gains after the Reserve Bank of India kept its policy repo rate unchanged, as expected, as it awaits data to judge whether higher oil prices are stoking domestic inflationary pressures. The currency was last seen at 95.03 a dollar.

Title: 'Like the end of the world': Eclipse chasers flocking to Spain
Article:
SUDDENLY, the world is plunged into an eerie, violet darkness. The temperature drops. Birds and other animals, bewildered by unforeseen night, start behaving strangely.
Stars and planets appear in the sky next to the blotted-out Sun.
It is this awe-inspiring experience that will draw people from all over the world to northern Spain next week in the hope of witnessing a total solar eclipse.
"It feels like it's the end of the world... you're changed forever if you see one," said Elizabeth Warning, one of four self-described "eclipse-chasers" who spoke to AFP ahead of the Aug 12 event.
However, with devastating fires still raging in some areas of Spain where the eclipse will be visible, the 51-year-old TV researcher may cancel her plans to travel from Sydney, Australia.
"It's very sad," Warning said. But as an Australian well-versed with the threat of bushfires, she said her heart went out to people in Spain mourning "lost houses and lost loved ones."
She is just one member of a small but growing community who plan holidays around seeing total solar eclipses, which take place every year or two.
Witnessing these remarkable events often requires intricate and expensive travel plans. However the total eclipse in Spain – the first visible in mainland Europe this century – is an easier trip than some in the past.
Ryan Milligan, a solar physicist at Queen's University Belfast in Northern Ireland, has travelled for 12 different eclipses, to places as far-ranging as Siberia, Chile and the Faroe Islands.
"A total eclipse is not something you see, it's something you experience," he told AFP.
"The temperature drops, the light and the shadows are all in the wrong place, the colours are muted, there's a 360 degree sunset, the animals go to sleep – these things you cannot convey to people through a picture or a video or a news article," Milligan said.
"It's that adrenaline rush of trying to experience all that within a few minutes that pushes us literally to go to the ends of the Earth."
Then once the brief thrill is over, the chasers start planning for their next hit.
[[nid:1504623]]
"It's a very expensive, very odd addiction," Warning said with a laugh.
Lucie Green went all the way to Antarctica in 2021, only to be thwarted by that common enemy of eclipse chasers: clouds.
"I've got about a two-thirds success rate," said the solar physicist at University College London.
Sometimes it works out. Warning described how the "the clouds parted" at the last second in the Faroe Islands in 2015, allowing her to see an eclipse that people just hundreds of metres away missed.
Milligan was one of those who saw only clouds.
"I was distraught... not least because they told me I would have seen it if I'd stayed in my hotel," he said.
Because they are travelling to the same place at the same time, members of this small community often meet up.
For example, while driving in the extremely remote northwest Australia to see an eclipse in 2019, Green said she bumped into Milligan.
For next week's eclipse, Jenny Winker, a 60-year-old retiree in St Paul, Minnesota, is travelling to northern Spain with nine other family members.
"If you've never seen a total eclipse, it is breathtaking," she said.
While watching smoke from wildfires in Canada drift over Minnesota, Winker said she has also been monitoring the Spanish fires.
Green explained that because the eclipse will occur just before sunset, particles from the fires could create a more "hazy" or "fuzzy" view.
Some chasers are already planning for a total eclipse next year that will be the longest humans will be able to see until 2114.
In Luxor, home to the Valley of the Kings in Egypt, the totality – when the Moon fully covers the Sun – will last six minutes and 22 seconds.
* The writer is from AFP

Title: Pakistani man charged with molesting woman in parked car in Batu Pahat
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A Pakistani perfume salesman was charged in the magistrate's court today with outraging the modesty of a woman he had recently met, inside a vehicle earlier this month.
Umair Iqbal Sheikh, 33, a father of three, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read before magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno.
He is accused of using criminal force with intent to outrage the modesty of a 26-year-old woman inside a parked car at Taman Sri Jaya at 4.30pm on Aug 1.
The charge was framed under Section 354 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of up to 10 years, a fine, or whipping, or any two of such punishments upon conviction.
The accused is said to have gotten to know the victim through social media before inviting her to meet.
As the victim was preparing to leave the vehicle, the accused allegedly molested her, leaving her shocked and frightened.
She later lodged a police report, which led to his arrest at about 7pm on the same day.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Shazleen Ibrahim appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was unrepresented.
The court granted bail at RM7,000 and set Sept 25 for mention for the submission of documents and appointment of lawyer.

Title: China's yuan hits its strongest in 3-1/2 years as trade tensions grow
Article:
SHANGHAI: China's yuan hit its strongest level in 3-1/2 years on Wednesday, as escalating trade and geopolitical tensions add to pressure for the currency to appreciate.
The Chinese currency was also bolstered by a softer dollar index, as easing Middle East tensions weakened the greenback's appeal. With the yuan under growing international scrutiny, "global policymakers appear increasingly aligned in discouraging competitive currency weakness," DBS said in a note.
On Wednesday, the onshore yuan changed hands at 6.7470 per dollar around noon time, having touched the strongest level since February 2023. The US dollar index slipped about 0.1 per cent. China is facing growing geopolitical risks as well as pressure over trade imbalances.
The Trump administration is preparing to set a price floor and impose tariffs on polysilicon and related products, seeking to protect US polysilicon factories from growing Chinese ambitions in the chip supply chain, sources told Reuters.
Washington is also drafting a ban on US imports of ⁠new ⁠models of Chinese data centre components on national security grounds, Reuters reported. Meanwhile, the US has joined hands with Japan to stabilise a falling yen, while the European Union is pressing China over alleged yuan undervaluation.
"Taken together, these developments reinforce the case for investors to pay closer attention to Asian currency appreciation than depreciation risks," DBS said. "This creates room for a broader recovery across Asian currencies."
Meanwhile, the dollar lost some luster on news that mediators were making progress in efforts to end the US-Iran war, driving oil prices lower. Ahead of the market open, China's central bank set the yuan's guidance rate at 6.7889 per dollar, also the strongest in 3-1/2 years.

Title: Selangor AI White Paper to outline landscape, address challenges - Amirudin
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor government's artificial intelligence (AI) White Paper, which is currently being developed, will outline the overall landscape for the use of the technology, including its challenges, benefits and value proposition.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the AI White Paper is the first policy on the technology to be developed by the state government and will be implemented in three phases, namely research and benchmarking, the drafting process, and the development of a Digital Government Playbook.
He said the document is intended to provide guidelines and ethical principles for the use of AI, while enabling a better understanding of the technology's challenges and benefits before it is adopted more widely.
"The AI White Paper will serve as a guideline for us, particularly in Selangor, on how we should approach, live with and interact with AI," he said.
He was responding to a question from Dr Quah Perng Fei (PH-Bandar Baru Klang) on the development of the AI landscape in Selangor at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly sitting today.
Amirudin said the AI White Paper would be tabled at the State Legislative Assembly for debate at a later date.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: College student held over newborn's death remanded for another day
Article:
KLUANG: A 19-year-old college student detained over the death of a newborn girl found in a toilet bowl at a house in Taman Setia Mutiara has been remanded for another day.
The Magistrate's Court granted the police extension to facilitate investigations under Section 302 and Section 315 of the Penal Code for murder and causing death after birth.
The suspect faces the death penalty or life imprisonment.
Kluang police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said the extension would allow police to complete their probe.
The suspect was arrested at 10.30pm after his girlfriend, who is also a college student, gave birth at the house.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad previously said police received a report that a female student had been admitted to Enche' Besar Hajjah Kalsom Hospital after giving birth.
Investigations revealed the student had delivered a baby and was found to still have another baby girl in her womb.
After giving birth, the student contacted her teacher before being taken to hospital for an examination.
Further investigations at the rented house occupied by the student led to the discovery of the body of a deceased baby girl.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hire more judges, boost training to cut court backlog, says former CJ
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Increasing the number of judges and ensuring continuous training are key to reducing the court backlog and strengthening judicial expertise in an increasingly complex world, former chief justice Tun Zaki Azmi said.
He said reforms introduced by Chief Justice Tun Wan Farid Wan Salleh reflect many of the measures implemented during his own tenure.
"He is introducing many of the same initiatives that I implemented during my time as chief justice; I increased the number of judges and provided training.
"The judges back then were almost angry with me because every Saturday and Sunday they had to attend courses on one subject or another.
"Judges must keep learning because no judge knows everything," he said at the 2nd Wisdom Malaysia 2026 Conference today.
Wan Farid had earlier called on the government to
consider
increasing the number of judicial officers, particularly in the lower courts, as part of broader reforms.
Zaki also expressed cautious support for the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the legal profession, stressing that it should only serve as a guide, with final decisions resting on human judgement.
The 81-year-old said he uses AI to broaden his thinking and generate ideas.
"I ask AI what I should say on a particular topic, and it gives me suggestions. But everything I have written here reflects my own views, 100 per cent.
"AI will never replace the human mind. It cannot replace human judgement, but what it can do is make people's work easier," he said.
He said that while lawyers could use AI as a starting point, they must always verify facts and scrutinise outputs for errors or "hallucinations".
Meanwhile, KerjayaOne PLT chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Mutalib Razak said the conference offers participants an opportunity to learn from veteran leaders through the sharing of practical leadership experience.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gamuda lands RM1.7bil hyperscale data centre job in Negri Sembilan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Gamuda Bhd has secured a RM1.71 billion contract from a United States-headquartered multinational technology company to build a hyperscale data centre in Port Dickson, Negri Sembilan.
The construction job was awarded to its subsidiary Gamuda Engineering Sdn Bhd, according to the company's bourse filing.
The project, which is on a build-only contract basis, involves constructing a single-storey hyperscale data centre facility comprising site infrastructure works, building core and shell construction, as well as mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) fit-out works.
Construction is scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2026, with completion targeted by the second quarter of 2028.
Gamuda said the project is expected to contribute to its revenue and earnings from the financial year ending July 31, 2027 until the project's completion.
It added that the project is subject to normal construction risks, including material price fluctuations, which will be mitigated through its experience and expertise in construction projects.

Title: Court to decide if Rosmah can defer RM67.5mil payment to Lebanese jeweller
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court has fixed Aug 12 to decide whether Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor can defer payment of RM67.5 million to Lebanese jewellery company Global Royalty Trading SAL.
Judicial Commissioner Marianne Antoinette Ghani fixed the date after hearing submissions from both sides today.
Rosmah was represented by lawyer Mohd Reza Rahim, while Global Royalty was represented by lawyer Venothani Rajagopal.
On June 10, High Court judge Datuk Quay Chew Soon ordered Rosmah, 75, to pay RM67.5 million to Global Royalty over 43 pieces of jewellery allegedly loaned to her.
The court ordered her to settle the sum within a month from the date of judgment.
In his judgment, Quay said the court found a prima facie case that Rosmah had failed to return the jewellery to Global Royalty, amounting to negligence.
He said Rosmah had failed to prove her claim that all 43 pieces had been seized by the authorities.
Quay also dismissed Rosmah's claim against the Inspector-General of Police and the government over her allegation that the missing jewellery had been seized during a police raid linked to investigations into the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) financial scandal in 2018.
The judge said Rosmah had maintained that the jewellery was handed to her for viewing under a consignment arrangement.
He said the authenticity of the consignment notes had never been disputed in earlier proceedings, adding that Rosmah herself had relied on and referred to the documents in advancing her case and giving evidence.
Global Royalty had filed a US$14.57 million suit against Rosmah over the loss of more than 40 pieces of jewellery allegedly loaned to her.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Three more arrested in MACC's Tabung Haji RCI probe over RM450,000 penalty notices
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested three more people in connection with its investigation into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH) over alleged misappropriation involving about RM450,000 in Notice of Penalty (NOP) charges.
The three male suspects, all in their 50s, comprise a deputy general manager for construction, an occupational safety and health manager, and a project director of a government-linked property company.
The company is a subsidiary of a statutory body.
An MACC source said the three were arrested at about 6pm yesterday after they turned up at the commission's headquarters to assist investigations.
Preliminary investigations found that the trio were believed to have conspired in the alleged offence between 2017 and 2019.
Following their arrest, the suspects were brought before Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah at the Putrajaya Magistrates' Court this morning, where a five-day remand order until Aug 9 was obtained.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests when contacted, adding that the case was being investigated under Section 17(a) of the MACC Act.
The latest arrests are part of
an investigation by the special task force
established to examine findings from the RCI into TH, which were made public on July 29.
On July 31, MACC launched its probe into the RCI report by sending an eight-member team to TH's headquarters to identify relevant documents and materials.
The Cabinet had earlier agreed to declassify and release the RCI report, which examined TH's management and operations between 2014 and 2020.
The RCI highlighted financial weaknesses linked to high hibah payments, investment risks, accounting issues and governance shortcomings.
Among its key findings, the commission said TH should have reported a RM1.4 billion loss in 2017 instead of the RM3.4 billion profit recorded in its financial statements after taking into account impairment losses and adjustments.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Poachers exploit northern border, Malayan tigers remain top target list
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's northern land border has become the main entry point for foreign poachers, particularly from Vietnam, seeking to hunt endangered wildlife, including the critically endangered Malayan tiger.
Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence (WCB/PSK) commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said syndicates use illegal border crossings to enter the country before moving into forest reserves believed to be home to their target species.
"Once inside, the poachers are prepared to remain deep in the forest for months, sometimes exceeding six months.
"During that time, they establish contacts with local syndicate members, accumulate wildlife products and smuggle them back to their home country, where demand is exceptionally high," he told Bernama.
He said the Malayan tiger, with an estimated wild population of only about 200, remains the syndicates' prime target as a single tiger can fetch up to RM500,000 on the black market.
Zaki said other targeted species include elephants, pangolins, deer, hornbills, exotic birds, reptiles and protected primates.
"Syndicates also traffic wildlife parts and derivatives such as ivory, pangolin scales, fangs, skins and other high-value body parts.
"The value of each species varies according to domestic and international demand, prompting continuous intelligence gathering and close cooperation with enforcement agencies to detect threats to protected wildlife," he said.
He said wildlife products are typically smuggled overseas, where demand and prices are significantly higher, particularly for exotic food and traditional medicine.
[[nid:1504584]]
"However, intelligence indicates demand has expanded beyond traditional medicine. Wildlife products are increasingly traded as collectibles, ornaments, accessories, trophies, luxury souvenirs and status symbols, while e-commerce platforms and social media have enabled more discreet cross-border transactions," he said.
Meanwhile, Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) director-general Datuk Abdul Kadir Abu Hashim said enforcement efforts have been intensified through integrated operations dubbed
Operasi Bersepadu Khazanah
(OBK) involving police, Customs Department, Forestry Department and relevant non-governmental organisations.
Since 2019, the OBK has removed 2,851 snares, arrested 1,230 individuals and seized wildlife-related items worth RM416.3 million.
"The OBK's biggest success came in 2023 with the dismantling of the country's largest wildlife trafficking syndicate involving Vietnamese nationals. Three offenders were fined RM128.9 million and sentenced to eight years and six months' imprisonment, among the harshest penalties imposed under the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010," he said.
He said to strengthen patrols and enforcement, Perhilitan has recruited 1,950 Community Rangers comprising mostly Orang Asli, as well as military veterans and civilians, under the Biodiversity Protection and Patrolling Programme this year.
"These rangers are deployed across 203 control posts, including joint posts with NGO partners, to patrol protected areas and permanent forest reserves, combating encroachment, illegal logging and wildlife poaching by both local and foreign offenders," he said.
Meanwhile, Kadir said Perhilitan is also developing an artificial intelligence-powered app to accelerate the analysis of camera trap data.
He said that such an app can identify wildlife species more quickly, including distinguishing individual Malayan tigers by their stripe patterns, improving population monitoring and conservation efforts.
"Perhilitan also uses satellite collars to track selected wildlife in real time, supporting an early warning system that alerts authorities and nearby communities when animals approach human settlements to reduce human-wildlife conflict," he said.
Other technologies include camera traps to monitor wildlife populations and detect forest intrusions, as well as drones for aerial surveillance of wildlife accident hotspots, he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: GOF seizes RM9.39mil worth of illegal e-waste in Ipoh raids
Article:
IPOH: The General Operations Force (GOF) Northern Brigade seized 120,220kg of electronic waste (e-waste) worth about RM9.39 million, along with processing machinery, during raids on three premises around Ipoh on Aug 3.
Its commander SAC Balveer Singh Mahindar Singh said the operation also led to the arrest of 14 people aged between 20 and 50, comprising two local men believed to be the premises managers and 12 Myanmar workers, including eight men and four women.
He said intelligence gathered over a week found that the three premises were allegedly processing e-waste without approval from the Department of Environment (DOE), while operating under the guise of recycling factories.
"The raiding team also found e-waste stored in jumbo bags and piled up inside and around the three premises," he told a press conference here today.
Balveer Singh said all the seized items had been handed over to the Perak DOE for investigation under Sections 18(1), 25(1), 34A and 34B of the Environmental Quality Act 1974.
He said the Immigration Department and the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) had also launched investigations under the Immigration Act 1959/63 and the Income Tax Act 1967, respectively.
Balveer Singh said the GOF would continue strengthening cooperation with relevant agencies to curb illegal e-waste processing and urged the public to report any suspicious activities involving e-waste to the authorities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MACC remands three more over alleged RM450,000 misuse of penalty payments
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 5 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has obtained a five-day remand order against three more individuals, including a deputy general manager for construction, an occupational safety and health manager, and a project director of a property company that is a subsidiary of a statutory body, over the alleged misappropriation of about RM450,000 in Notice of Penalty (NOP) charges.
Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah issued the remand order until Aug 9 against the three men, who are in their 50s, following an application by the MACC at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court today.
According to a MACC source, the three were arrested at the commission’s headquarters at about 6 pm yesterday.
“Preliminary investigations found that the suspects allegedly conspired to commit the offence between 2017 and 2019,” the source said.
The source said the arrests followed investigations by a special task force set up to examine the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Tabung Haji, which were made public through the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia’s (JAKIM) official portal on July 29.
Meanwhile, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests and said the case was being investigated under Section 17(a) of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: High Court acquits temple chairman over alleged trespass at Sri Maha Mariamman temple
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 5 — The High Court today acquitted a temple chairman who had been charged with trespassing at the Sri Maha Mariamman Temple on privately owned land last year,
Sinar Harian
reported.
Lawyer Latheefa Koya, who represented M Paramaguru, 49, said Justice Hazlina Hussain quashed the charge after finding it was fatally defective.
In a statement, Latheefa said the court ruled the charge failed to disclose the criminal intent required to constitute the offence of trespass.
According to the news report, she said the judge found the charge did not state that Paramaguru, who is also a security guard, had the necessary intent to satisfy the elements of criminal trespass.
The court also held that proceeding with the trial would only waste judicial time, she added.
Latheefa said the prosecution had argued the element of intent could be established during the trial, but the court disagreed.
On Feb 9, Paramaguru pleaded not guilty in the Sepang Magistrate’s Court to trespassing on land owned by Datuk Suhaili Ahmad in Dengkil on June 19, 2025.
He was charged under Section 447 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of six months, a fine of up to RM3,000, or both, upon conviction.
